prerequisites: Knowledge of topics covered in Calculus I (Analisi Matematica I) courses is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Describe the main concepts and tools of applied economics for engineering.
Understand the decision-making mechanisms of companies.
Apply basic economic models to the analysis of simple business and industrial problems.
Use the main economic-financial indicators in investment evaluation.
Compare different economic alternatives based on available data and information.
Clearly present concepts and results of analyses performed.
Independently deepen the topics covered using indicated texts and teaching materials.

syllabus_topics: Behavior of companies in different institutional contexts.
Economic decisions under certainty and uncertainty.
Functioning of markets and main resource allocation mechanisms.
Relationships between production choices and economic results.
Analysis of economic and financial flows.
Main decision criteria for investment evaluation.
Evaluation of the economic convenience of investment projects.
assessment_rules: Students have the option to take an intermediate test on the first part of the course. If passed, the final exam will only cover the second part. The final written exam consists of 7-10 exercises with multiple application and/or theoretical questions. Students can take the oral exam in the same session they pass the written exam. Oral questions cover topics not clearly answered in the written exam and other program topics not covered in the written exam.
